Unbeaten in five career outings, the daughter of Night Of Thunder only ever seems to do enough and the way she finished off the 1000 Guineas gave a strong indication that she may relish this rise in distance. A taking winner of the Cheshire Oaks, Minnie Hauk must enter calculations as a proven stayer but the best of the Ballydoyle contingent may be Whirl, who produced a career-best performance when landing the Musidora at York. Hailing from a family that includes Oaks winner Look Here, Revoir is another to consider on the rise in trip, as is the supplemented Elwateen, who caught the eye on only her second start when a highly-encouraging fourth in the Guineas.

selections.comment: STEDE BONNET has a smart pedigree and showed nice ability on debut. A sibling to seven winners, including course bumper winner Shannon Royale, the selection was headed close home by the more experienced winner at Kilbeggan last month. Being a four-year-old, he should continue to progress and can put that experience to good use. By a leading jumps stallion, her Flat-bred dam notably is a half-sister to Racing Post Trophy/Dante winner Dilshaan so she could have plenty of pace. Cooladdi was in strong contention when falling at the second-last in an April point-to-point and it is encouraging that he contests a bumper.

Kartayaz, who was placed in Sligo, and Roman Harry, who travelled well before being outgunned in second in a Tipperary claimer, are others with chances.

selections.comment: The lightly raced TOP TIER GOSSIP ran well when 3rd on hurdle debut last time out at Worcester, albeit she was a little keen throughout. However, she is in very capable hands here with the Skeltons, and with that much-needed experience under her belt, she can very much take a step forward and win a race of this nature. The Irish raider Herja arrives into this contest after a fine 2nd at Ffos Las last time out over 2m6f; although well beaten, she clearly did not stay the step up in trip and could be a threat to the Skelton horse here. She sets the standard off the mark of 107 but would need a career best to win this. Solent Gateway is a very consistent sort and has the hurdling experience, but is 0 for 5 over obstacles, so he might have to settle with filling the places once again.

selections.comment: Full Monty was a very decent 2nd on chase debut over 2m4f at Worcester last time out, and with just the 1lb rise in the weights, he could go one better here. However, Alan King's BASKERVILLE was mightily impressive when well backed for his chase debut at Stratford 19 days ago. Prominent throughout the race, he didn't jump with too much fluency but clearly has a real engine and soon powered clear by an easy 12-length win in the end with some experienced chasers in behind. He does have an 8lb rise in the weights to deal with here; however, given the nature of how he won last time out, it looks like he could go in again. Lune De La Mer makes his chase debut after a good 2nd over hurdles last time out, but he would have to put in a career best to beat the main two with chasing experience.

With ten wins in just thirty-three career starts over fences under his belt and a length win at Cartmel last time, he can go in again here off just a 2lb higher mark. Finest View is the unexposed one who arrives into this contest with just the three career starts under her belt; she was a pretty impressive winner at Huntingdon last time out when well fancied in the market, so she is the one to look out for. Famoso is 2lb lower than his last winning mark and did place twice a few runs back; this sort of trip will more than suit, and he could be the one to fill the placings.

However, a repeat of that effort could see him win this race in what on paper seems to be a slightly easier contest than last time out. Tropical Talent has bags of experience having run over both hurdles and fences, and now off a career-low mark of 80, he could build on that 2nd placed effort over fences in April. Portcammon was a bumper winner for the all-conquering Willie Mullins, so clearly has talent. But needs to find that for new connections and trainer Neil Mulholland.

A combined winner of 9 and 1/4 lengths in her last two races, judging by the way she comfortably landed the last contest just 9 days ago, she looks to still be very much ahead of the handicapper at present. She will have to deny the career-high mark here; however, given the fact of how in-form she is, it should not be a surprise if she wins her third race in a row. Lipa K has been mixing it up over hurdles and fences, and albeit it was over the larger obstacles, he is a pound lower than his last winning mark at this track back in May 2024. Liverpool Knight has been running well and runs off his last winning mark here, with the stable's main jockey deciding to ride him instead of the yard's other runner.

Danny Giligan wasn't really pushing her that hard when she came down, and all being well in a slightly easier race, she can finally get her head in front. Her mark of 90 looks to be a fairly lenient one, and she can take full advantage of that here. Heather Honey has been in flying form at present as she looks to land the hat trick of victories but does have the 6lb climb in the weights to deal with here as she comes up against some very unexposed types in this company. Newmill Getaway was a decent 2nd on her stable debut for Fergal O'Brien last time out, and she could improve a little more with this step up in trip.

selections.comment: A very open affair with a case to be made for most. Dembe would be the selection if this were on the AW but his turf form falls way short of his AW form and he is overlooked, along with Viennoise where similar comments apply. KING OF CHARM gets the nod, arriving here on the back of an encouraging pipe-opener and with some scope for improvement. He can add a third career success to the CV. One to take the eye at likely bigger odds is Mudamer who found 7f the last twice a bit on the sharp side and should be more comfortable back at a mile like at Ripon three starts back when just touched off. He's due to go down a pound in the future so some will be put off but it should give a little juice to his price and a bold bid is expected. Another who needs to take a step forward on his latest run is Eligible who never got into the race off a break at York over 7f. Back at a mile he can show his best and is entitled to go close if near peak and can fill the frame ahead of Lerwick, who should not be underestimated but needs to shrug off two poor recent turf runs

He showed good promise on the All-weather in between, winning twice and second the other two runs. The latest win came on handicap bow on penultimate start where he looked as if there was plenty more in the locker. Up The pace won that Ascot race with the selection almost five lengths behind and has obvious claims to double up. However, he was 33/1 that day and while no fluke it was a significant step forward and he may prove vulnerable off 5lb extra. Philanthropist couldn't quite handle the jump up to class 2 to complete the hat-trick last time but now back at this level can prove a serious threat again

selections.comment: This looks trappy as there are doubts in one way or another about practically every runner, bar the dependable Diego Ventura, who looks sure to go well. That said, a 3lb penalty for his narrow last-time-out Listed win in France leaves the door ajar for something or other to beat him with the suggestion being Charlie Appleby's HALLASAN, whose peak form - including a defeat of Camille Pissarro no less in a big sales race at Doncaster last season - entitles him to have a very big say. Rebel's Diamond may be third best ahead of the reappearing filly Saqqara Sands, for whom market confidence would be significant.

Both of them were disadvantaged in sitting off a less than frenetic pace at Meydan last time, particularly Giavellotto, who was dropped in in order to try and offset a wide draw but never remotely got involved. Jan Brueghel is best of the other five and can claim minor honours.

selections.comment: Only nine runners but an up-to-scratch renewal with a host of highly promising trial winners taking on a proven Group 1 filly. That filly is of course the unbeaten Desert Flower who will be tough to beat if she does stay this longer trip while the way she found plenty late on when taking the 1,000 Guineas last time again augured well for her staying further than 1m. Her pedigree does raise enough of a doubt though for preference to be for an each-way alternative at bigger odds. That brings in WHIRL, who was a revelation when running away with the Musidora at York last time, is highly likely to stay 1m4f and can continue Aidan O'Brien's superb record of late in this race. She wouldn't be the first filly which is ostensibly the stable second string to win this either. Stablemate Giselle can claim minor honours ahead of potential improvers Elwateen and Ryan Moore's pick of the O'Brien trio, Minnie Hauk.
